newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco, Canada to expand fish cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Morocco, Canada to expand fish cooperation.

text.p: Morocco and Canada signed a fisheries accord on Tuesday to reinforce technical cooperation and expertise, the official MAP news agency reported.
"The accord will cover ways to preserve fish stocks, promote products, exchange information and expertise on fisheries techniques and shipbuilding," the agency said.
Canada and Morocco recently signed an agreement to set up a regional training centre for fishery development on the Atlantic coast near the southern city of Agadir, MAP added.
Morocco plans to invest 1.3 billion dirhams ($141 million) over four years to upgrade its fishing industry and infrastructure, the fisheries ministry said.
Morocco's fish exports rose to the equivalent of $886 million in 1996 against $749 million in 1995.
Morocco received in the same period an extra $150 million as royalties to allow the E.U. 750-ship fishing fleet into its rich waters, the ministry added.
